item.title: Watch: 2026 Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane makes Virat Kohli admission after 'starstruck' question
item.description: England footballer Harry Kane was asked about whether he was left "starstruck" by any congratulatory message following his historic Ballon d'Or victory. The striker revealed he had recieved multiple messages from sportspersons, including Indian cricket legend Virat Kohli . "People like David Beckham, who is a big idol of mine, have messaged me. Tom Brady, Virat Kohli, you know..a lot of sports people I really admire and look up to," Kane told reporters. Watch: — Melbourne__82 (@Melbourne__82) Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or at a ceremony held at the London Palladium on October 26, becoming the first English footballer in 25 years to receive the prestigious award. The Bayern Munich striker narrowly beat Kylian Mbappé, collecting 1,055 points compared to the Frenchman's 1,027. Lamine Yamal was also among the leading contenders. The England captain enjoyed an outstanding 2025-26 season, scoring 73 goals across all competitions for Bayern Munich. His performances helped him secure the biggest individual honour in football. However, a special message from Kohli made the occasion even more memorable for him. Harry Kane reveals Virat Kohli's special message Kane admitted that receiving congratulations from Kohli was a surprising and memorable moment. Despite being one of football's biggest stars himself, he was impressed to hear from the Indian batter, whom he has admired for a long time. Kohli is widely regarded as one of the greatest cricketers of his generation. His popularity extends beyond cricket, with several international sporting personalities recognising his achievements and influence. The Indian star's famous unbeaten 82 off 51 balls against Australia in the 2016 T20 World Cup remains one of the most memorable performances of his career. His ability to deliver under pressure has earned him admirers across different sports. How did Kane and Kohli develop mutual respect? The connection between Kane and Kohli goes back several years. The two sporting icons reportedly met in London in May 2019, helping establish a mutual admiration for each other's achievements. Kohli's congratulatory message was therefore more than just a routine gesture for Kane. It came from someone he genuinely respects and admires. Kohli's popularity among international sporting stars is not new. American football legend Tom Brady has also previously spoken about the Indian cricketer's appeal.

item.title: Green Bay Packers receive encouraging Micah Parsons update ahead of Patriots matchup
item.description: The Green Bay Packers found their footing again in Week 8, earning a 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers. Their defense led the way, and the unit could receive another boost following the team’s latest injury update. Micah Parsons could soon take another step toward returning to the field. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Monday the team is preparing for the star pass rusher to resume practicing this week. Parsons has not played since Green Bay’s December 14, 2025, matchup with Denver, when he suffered a torn ACL. He has been focused on recovering from the injury ever since. Having Parsons back for Sunday’s matchup with the Patriots would give Green Bay a major lift. Still, his expected return to practice does not necessarily mean he will be cleared for game action right away. Reports have pointed to the Packers’ Thanksgiving Eve meeting with the Rams as a more realistic target for his return. Will Micah Parsons finally return for the Green Bay Packers? Green Bay Packers defensive end Parsons (1), linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (56) and cornerback Keisean Nixon (25) team up to stop Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) on Sunday, September 7, 2025, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. The Packers won the game, 27-13. Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin The timing would work in Green Bay’s favor, as the Packers have their bye week immediately before that matchup. A return to practice this week would give Parsons several weeks to build up before potentially being activated for Week 12. Although he would miss a significant portion of the season, he could still appear in seven regular season games. Even with that limited window, Parsons could provide a major boost as Green Bay pushes for a playoff spot. Green Bay Packers defensive end Parsons (1) interacts with fans before a game against the Chicago Bears on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 31-7. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Green Bay enters the stretch run with a 5-3 record and remains in contention for the NFC North title, despite sitting fourth in the division. The Packers’ Week 10 clash with the Minnesota Vikings could prove crucial as they look to strengthen their position in the NFC playoff race. The Packers will be looking to secure an important win this weekend, regardless of whether Parsons is available. Parsons and the Packers visit the Patriots on November 8, with kickoff set for 4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium. item.title: Ranking the Rockies, 2026: No. 29, Gabriel Hughes
item.description: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 18: Colorado Rockies pitcher Gabriel Hughes (43) pitches in the first inning during a game between the Seattle Mariners and the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field on September 18, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to the 2026 edition of Ranking the Rockies, where we take a look back at every player to log playing time for the Rockies in 2026. The purpose of this list is to provide a snapshot of the player in context. The “Ranking” is an organizing principle that’s drawn from Baseball Reference’s WAR (rWAR). It’s not something the staff debated. We’ll begin with the player with the lowest rWAR and end up with the player with the highest. No. 29, Gabriel Hughes (0.1 rWAR) When the Colorado Rockies selected Gabriel Hughes 10th overall out of Gonzaga in the 2022 MLB Draft , they knew they were taking on a power arm with at least a middle-of-the-rotation ceiling. However, after Tommy John surgery cut his 2023 season short and kept him out of the 2024 season, he had to start building his stock in 2025. Hughes had a solid season last year, despite dealing with several injuries throughout the year. Heading into 2026, it seemed like it was inevitable that he would finally reach the big leagues. He finally earned his call-up to the big leagues in early July 2026 , making his Major League debut on July 3 against the San Francisco Giants. His inaugural taste of the majors was predictably turbulent. Across 14 games (13 starts) for Colorado, Hughes posted a 6.33 ERA and an 0-8 record. On paper, those surface-level traditional figures look grim. However, a closer look under the hood reveals a far more nuanced picture of a young arm navigating his initial trial by fire. Triple-A momentum After a solid, albeit limited, spring training audition, Hughes was sent to Triple-A Albuquerque to start the 2026 campaign. He got off to a rough start, posting an 8.64 ERA in 25 innings across six starts. The strikeouts weren’t an issue as he had 32 against just six walks, but he was giving up a lot of contact and getting hit hard. At the end of April, he was placed on the injured list and missed most of May. After a pair of strong rehab starts with High-A Spokane, Hughes was sent back to the Isotopes where he looked like a man possessed. Over his next three starts in June, Hughes allowed just four hits across 15.2 innings with 16 strikeouts and five walks, limiting opponents to a .080/.179/.100 slash. His best outing of the year at any level came on June 25 when he fired six shutout innings at home against the Salt Lake Bees, giving up just two hits while striking out six. It was hard to ignore that Hughes had tapped into something while recovering from injury, and he had suddenly tamed the Pacific Coast League. item.title: Who is more to blame, the Cowboys offense or the defense?
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Cowboys fans and fans across the country. This week, we wanted to know which side of the ball you are blaming more for the absolutely crushing loss against the Arizona Cardinals. We’ll make a case for and against each unit and then we’ll hit the polls for a vote. For blaming the offense: The Dallas Cowboys came into the season knowing the offense needed to carry the team. The defense was the defense, so the offense had to be elite. Remember GOTI? More like goat, and not the good kind. The offense has so many chances to put the game away but they couldn’t do it. Having CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the sidelines during crucial plays is never a good look. Wasted points allowed the Cardinals to hang around. Against blaming the offense: They scored 30 points. In the NFL, that is usually a winning number. They handed the defense a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter, and a 10-point lead late in the fourth quarter. It’s hard to ask for more than that from an NFL offense. They may not have played great, but they provided margins in the fourth quarter anyone would have taken before the game. For blaming the defense: It’s hard to comprehend the collapse of the Cowboys defense the minute Gardner Minshew stepped onto the field. He and Tyler Allgeier shredded the defense in a way that is mathematically improbable. They gave up 27 points in a 16.5-minute stretch to end regulation. Absurd. Against blaming the defense: We know the Cowboys defense is bad, but the Cowboys offense and coaching kept making decisions like they’re good. Instead of running up the score early when the defense was balling, they only put up 14 points in the first half. The offense kept the Cardinals in the game in the second half with conservative decisions. And at least the defense was playing against Minshew/Allgeier, a combo they hadn’t prepared for. The offense doesn’t have that excuse. Hit the polls below and then tell us your thoughts in the comments. Who is to blame for the loss? Are you confident in the Cowboys? item.title: Liverpool v Arsenal: Two Penalties, But What About the Red Cards? – Opinion
item.description: Liverpool v Arsenal: Two Penalties, But What About the Red Cards? – Opinion Ankle Breakers, Head Slapping, and All the Media Want to Concentrate On Is a Non-Contact Headbutt, the Dive That Followed and Two Shirt Pulls!! Yes, it’s happening again, an over-the-top reaction to what The Arsenal did during the game with Liverpool. Let’s make it very clear that I agree the referee and VAR officials should have awarded a penalty, and they also missed another possible spot kick involving Tzolis. But here’s where I find the coverage of the game so one-sided and biased. If the penalties had been given, no player would have been under the threat of a long-term injury or sent off for violent conduct, resulting in a minimum three-match ban, unlike the laughable reaction to a “headbutt” that would also have resulted in a three-match violent conduct ban!! Both Arsenal players could have been booked, but that would have been the maximum possible outcome regarding the penalties. What About the Challenges on Odegaard? However, the second-minute tackle on Odegaard was one that could be seen as a career-threatening injury, and yet no action was taken, as happened when the same player should have received another yellow card just ten minutes later. Which of these four incidents should have been called out and covered by the media, simply because of the violence shown and the long-term consequences? Then we have the farce of Odegaard yet again being targeted for physical assault, when he was slapped around the head after being fouled once again by a player who then decided to fake a headbutt in order to get another player sent off. Why are these incidents not being reported and investigated with the same scrutiny that an obvious shirt pull has been? Where Is the Balance in the Media Coverage? I feel that all four incidents should have involved the VAR officials, and Liverpool should have had two penalties awarded regarding two of them. However, Liverpool should have been down to ten men as early as the second minute, if not by the fifteenth minute, while ending the game with nine men!! Slapping someone around the head is violent conduct and a red card, while faking a headbutt should be a yellow card. So let’s get these four incidents into perspective and rise above the usual media-biased hype against our club. By the way, although the officials had a bad day at the office, at least they didn’t favour either team. item.title: Diamondbacks Need More Luck
item.description: Inspiration. In the last three seasons, the Diamondbacks failed to make the playoffs. They failed with 89 wins, they failed with 80 wins, and they failed with 86 wins. They were so very close. Why did they fall short? Every day, Torey Lovullo thinks about possible ways to improve the Diamondbacks. Many players strive to stack one percent improvements. And yet it wasn’t enough. Why? First Thoughts. One thought is that people more often find what they look for than what they are not looking for. The Diamondbacks are looking for improvements. Is it that simple? No. Another thought is that being optimistic helps people focus on good outcomes instead of bad outcomes. Perhaps focusing on good outcomes makes them more likely. Is it that simple? Although that is part of the answer, no. Perhaps the Diamondbacks need more luck. Luck has long been seen as significant. “Again I saw that under the sun the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor riches to the intelligent, nor favor to the men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.” — Ecclesiastes 9:11 What is luck? Luck is when the underdog Diamondbacks win games against strong teams, especially when the reasons are a combination of small things that are not apparent beforehand. One example was that in July the Diamondbacks swept the Dodgers in a three game series. Recently underdog wins happened many times each season! What specifically can the Diamondbacks do to make more good luck happen? One approach is flexibility to try different things, with recognition to quickly know what is working, and continuing what works (at least until it doesn’t). This could be called trial and error. It would be very lucky if this approach got the Diamondbacks to the playoffs. A better approach is to search for improvement ideas, implement some of the ideas, with recognition to quickly know whether each improvement is worth continuing, Instead of narrowly, search broadly for improvement ideas. This idea about improvements extends a previous idea about baseball players that I found years ago. On the baseball field, the best baseball players have a narrow focus on their tasks AND a broad focus on everything relevant that could impact their task. Instead of only a group of insiders, also talk with trusted outsiders who are wise and tell them what you are searching for. Keep searching for improvement ideas. If one idea turns out to be spectacularly great, don’t let it stop the search. If one idea fails, don’t let it stop the search. The best improvements to implement have small downsides, so that you can survive one or two failures. Although the upsides may be small, the improvement process can continue despite failures. Some improvements give the player (or the team) choices that can address situations that can occur in specific games, even if the situations are relatively rare. item.description: UAlbany's Ollie Engen looks to pass during a Monday, Nov. 2 game against Rhode Island College at Broadview Center in Albany. (Provided by UAlbany Athletics) ALBANY - Ollie Engen had no problem getting to the rim or pulling up for floaters in the paint early on in the University at Albany men's basketball season opener Monday night at Broadview Center. The junior guard just couldn't get those early looks to fall. So, after Engen missed his first four shots, coach Dwayne Killings took him out and gave him some advice. "Told him, ‘Just settle down,'" Killings said. "I thought he shorted two of his first shots. They were below the rim. I was just like, ‘finish higher above (the rim).'" Once Engen re-entered the game, he looked far more like the high-scoring player who was a U Sports second-team All-Canadian player last season at Queen's University in Ontario. He made 12 of his final 17 shots en route to a 25-point outing as he provided one of the bright spots in a 74-67 win over Division III Rhode Island College that was too close for comfort for Killings, Engen and the rest of the Great Danes. Engen, the Great Danes' 6-foot-5 point guard, also had six assists and grabbed five rebounds. He played a big part in UAlbany cruising to a 28-point lead with 13:11 left in the second half, but also took responsibility for many of the offensive struggles and defensive errors down the stretch that allowed the Anchormen to make what had looked to be a runaway UAlbany win into a far closer game than anticipated. item.title: Dad texted daughter 'go easy' before NYC Marathon runner’s death
item.description: Rachel Apa, 24, was about seven miles into the New York City Marathon on Nov. 1 when she texted her father for the first time on the course. "She said, 'Never felt better. I must have done the carb loading correctly for the first time,'" her father, Steve Apa, said. But 17 miles later – just two from the finish line – Rachel Apa collapsed. She was pronounced dead hours later. Steve Apa said his daughter was diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis , a rare injury that causes muscle breakdown and is usually caused by overexertion, according to the Cleveland Clinic. The New York Police Department confirmed to USA TODAY that a 24-year-old female experienced a "medical episode" near mile marker 24 and was transported to the hospital in critical condition. The marathon was Rachel Apa's first. She ran it for the Parkinson's Foundation after her paternal grandfather died from the disease. "My grandfather was my role model growing up. He taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges, shaping my love for sports and movement," she wrote on a fundraising page. New York Road Runners, which organizes the race, said in a statement: "We are deeply saddened by Rachel’s passing following running in Sunday’s race. Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with her family, friends, and the entire running community." More: What running does for your body Rachel Apa was a lifelong athlete, father says Rachel Apa, a native of Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, was a lifelong athlete and former field hockey player at Bucknell University, her father said. "She did everything she's supposed to for the training up to the marathon," Steve Apa said. "I remember her telling me, 'Dad, this weekend's my 18-mile run.' So she was fully trained, fully prepared." While Steve Apa was at home in Pennsylvania tracking his daughter on the marathon app, his wife, Michelle Apa, was along the route. He was texting her throughout the race. "I said, 'This is your first marathon. Go easy. Don't go out too fast,'" he said. "And then, every mile, I would just text her the mile number." Around mile 18, she texted him, "Ugh" and then "Ow," he said. "I said, 'go easy,' and then I pinged her when she hit the 20th mile and she said, 'ow,'" Steve Apa said. That was the last time he heard from her. At mile 23, Steve Apa sent his daughter another text: "Final stretch. Finished, not speed." Michelle Apa was waiting for her daughter around mile 25 when they noticed she appeared to have stopped moving on the tracking app. When she headed to mile 24, spectators told her an ambulance had just taken Rachel Apa to the hospital. A spectator later told Steve and Michelle Apa that they saw Rachel collapse and immediately began giving her CPR before eventually trying a defibrillator. She was then taken by ambulance to Mount Sinai Hospital where doctors worked on her from about 2 to 9 p.m. local time, Steve Apa said. item.title: King's Academy volleyball advances to first state final since 2007
item.description: King's Academy volleyball is headed to its first state championship match since 2007. The Lions swept Pensacola Catholic (25-23, 25-20, 25-20) to advance to the Class 3A state final at Polk State College in Winter Haven, Florida. "We're pumped," said King's Academy head coach Bethany Avila. "We've been working toward this all year long, just tried to stay humble and take one game at a time and work really hard in practice." The game was a straight sweep, but it was not without its challanges. Though King's Academy looked dominant for most of the first set, the No. 2 seed Lions had to survive a late 7-1 run by Pensacola Catholic and then revisit the court after a match point was overturned before finally putting away the Crusaders for the early match lead. Pensacola Catholic didn't make things much easier as the morning went on. The Crusaders were forced into an early timeout in the second set after King's Academy seized momentum, but they recovered with their own run and would tie the set at 11-11. But the Lions were able to overcome challenges the rest of the way, thanks in large part to their dominant presence in the middle. With 54 blocks heading into the state semifinal, freshman Yasmin Nunes shined on the biggest stage with her presence in the middle. So, too, did junior newcomer Anabelle Bencosme on the outside. "They both fly under the radar because they're new," Avila said. "They're kind of our secret weapons, but they're not so secret anymore. They have super high verticals that they've been working on this year and that is what has elevated their game both literally and figuratively." Between Nunes and Jordan Molnar, King's Academy was ready for almost every play at the net. and Molnar, who is King's Academy's setter, does just about everything well. "Jordan Molnar was on fire as far as her blocking," Avila said. "I know she is our setter, but she is also our top blocker and she shut down their outside, and she stepped in and blocked their middles, too. She just knows how to get a point." King's Academy has won three state championships, but the most recent came in 2006, 20 years ago. The Lions are ready to end that drought, but to do so, they will have to face off against the winner of No. 1 Merritt Island and No. 4 Pine Crest, who began their state semifinal at 1 p.m. Alex Peterman is a high school sports reporter for The Palm Beach Post. item.title: NYC Marathon Runner Rachel Apa, 24, Dies Just 2 Miles From Finish Line During First Race
item.description: Bucknell University Rachel Apa had a special reason for taking on the New York City Marathon. The 24-year-old was running in honor of her late grandfather, who passed away from Parkinson’s disease. Tragically, Apa never made it to the finish line as she collapsed and died. Apa collapsed near Mile 24 of Sunday’s race, just two short miles from the finish line in Central Park. This was her first marathon, and she was participating as part of the Parkinson’s Champions team to raise money for research, according to The New York Times . Her family was cheering her on along the sidelines as she made her way through the marathon. Her mother, Michelle, was following along in person, while her father, Steve, tracked her progress from home. The race appeared to be going well, as Apa reportedly told her father early in the race that she had never felt better. However, her messages became more concerning as she complained of pain. She eventually sent a message saying she was in the final stretch, just before collapsing. A bystander began to perform CPR as soon as they noticed Apa, and then medical personnel took over. Medical staff continued lifesaving efforts and used an automated external defibrillator before EMS arrived. EMS transported Apa to Mount Sinai Medical Center, but despite their best efforts, she died later that evening in the hospital. Apa was a former Division I field hockey player at Bucknell University. Her father, Steve, described her as being in excellent health and stated that she had trained and prepared for this marathon. Her father also told The New York Times that he believed his daughter died from rhabdomyolysis, a potentially life-threatening condition that involved the breakdown of muscle tissue. However, the NYC medical examiner said that the cause of death has yet to be determined. In a statement from New York Road Runners, which organized this marathon, they stated that they were deeply saddened by Apa’s passing and extended their condolences to her family, friends, and the running community. item.description: Texans general manager Nick Caserio faces a consequential decision at next Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. (Melissa Phillip/Houston Chronicle) It happens every year. The NFL's trade deadline comes around and teams are forced to confront a major question at the midpoint of their season. Do they sacrifice the future for immediate help in hopes of competing for a Super Bowl? Do they start over and sell off assets as they plan for the future? Or do they stay put? That's where the Houston Texans sit one week before the Nov. 10 trade deadline as general manager Nick Caserio confronts those questions. Since coach DeMeco Ryans arrived nearly four years ago, Caserio and the Texans have taken a measured approach to the trade deadline. They haven't quite been buyers and they definitely haven't been sellers. They've mostly stayed quiet during this crucial part of the season, though it hasn't always been for a lack of trying. Last season, the Texans called the Jets about running back Breece Hall , but felt the asking price - a third-round pick - was too high. This year will more than likely be more of the same. Bennett/Getty; Michael Owens/Getty NEED TO KNOW Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell said linebacker Jack Campbell is “improving” after he suffered a serious neck injury on Nov. 1 “It’s not easy because he’s always going to be on our minds over here,” Dan said on 97.1 The Ticket Jack has remained hospitalized since the collision Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell provided an update on linebacker Jack Campbell’s condition after the Pro Bowler suffered a serious neck injury on Sunday, Nov. 1. During an interview with 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday, Nov. 3, the Lions head coach said Jack, 26, is “improving” as he remains hospitalized. The team confirmed that the former first-round pick sustained a neck injury in the second half of the Lions’ 19-15 home win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. “It’s not easy because he’s always going to be on our minds over here,” Dan, 50, told the radio show, adding, “The good news is he is improving.” Dan Campbell; Jack Campbell on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026 Credit: Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty; Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Dan said “knowing he’s doing better,” in reference to Jack, and keeping the other Lions players informed on the positive updates “helps everybody just get a better handle on this.” The head coach added, “All we can do at this point is just continue to pray for Jack, put our thoughts on him when we have a minute, and on his family — and it’s working, like I said, because he’s improving.” Dan asked for continued prayers for Jack. “Please continue to do that. Hockenson’s hip when he went to make a tackle in the fourth quarter. Jack landed face-first on the turf at Ford Field and remained motionless for several moments. item.title: Braves Lock In Acuña And Albies At Shocking Bargain Prices
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The biggest shock in Atlanta sports news isn’t a trade or a star leaving town. It is how little money the Atlanta Braves will pay their two best players next year. The team exercised their options for Ronald Acuña Jr and Ozzie Albies for the 2027 season, locking them in for a combined total of just $24 million. That figure is shockingly low for two players who have carried the franchise for a decade. Most fans expected a massive price tag for the 2023 NL MVP and the long-time second baseman. Instead, the club secured Acuña for $17 million and Albies for $7 million. This move was the “no-brainer decision of all no-brainer decisions” after the team won 94 games and claimed the NL East title, according to Battery Power . The organization also cleared the books by reinstating four pitchers from the injured list, including Spencer Strider and Hurston Waldrep, just as the postseason kicked off. The Price Tag Defies Logic It is rare to see a team keep its core stars for such a low cost in modern baseball. Acuña is set to make $6 million less than the standard MLB qualifying offer, which is a massive win for the front office. Some fans thought Acuña would not return, but those rumors ignored the reality of the contract signed years ago. The deal allows Atlanta to keep the player who achieved the historic 40-home run, 70-stolen base season in 2023. Ozzie Albies brings a similar value with his $7 million price tag for the upcoming year. While he had a career low in wRC+ this season, the team views him as a bridge for younger prospects waiting in Double-A. Replacing him would likely cause more trouble than simply keeping him on the roster for one more year. The financial flexibility this creates is huge for the rest of the roster. With $24 million committed to two All-Stars, the team has room to address other needs like shortstop. The Braves are looking at trade options such as Jeremy Peña from the Astros, as their current plans with Ha-Seong Kim did not work out. This budget allows them to be aggressive in the market while keeping their stars. Health Remains the Only Wild Card The only question left for both players is their physical status heading into next season. Acuña tore his ACL in 2024 but returned in 2025, proving he can still dominate when healthy. When he is not healthy, people hear about it constantly, but the team is betting on his recovery. The same logic applies to Albies, whose value skyrockets when he is on the field and playing his usual style. Reinstating the pitching staff shows the team is ready to move forward with a full squad. Neither Spencer Schwellenbach nor Spencer Strider should be anticipated to immediately resume their previous performance levels. Joey Wentz suffered a lower body injury blowing out his right ACL during a Spring Training bunt attempt.
